'''Olga Botner''' is a professor of experimental [[particle physics]] at [[Uppsala University]] known for her work on [[neutrino]]s. She is an elected member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]]. From 2013 until 2017 she was the spokesperson for the [[IceCube Neutrino Observatory]].

== Education and career ==
Botner received her [[candidate (degree)]] from the [[University of Copenhagen]] in 1978. She earned her Ph.D. in 1985 from the University of Copenhagen.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Olga Botner CV |url=https://www.uu.se/download/18.4d906724195b2636a1f2854d/1742861420715/XX2728.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250616033553/https://www.uu.se/download/18.4d906724195b2636a1f2854d/1742861420715/XX2728.pdf |archive-date=2025-06-16 |access-date=2025-06-16 |website=Uppsala University}}</ref>

After receiving her Ph.D., Botner worked at [[CERN]] on the Axial Field Spectrometer experiment at the Intersecting Storage Rings, which included calorimetry and quark flavor detection. She then worked on [[charm quark]] identification with the ring imaging Cherenkov counter placed in the [[UA2 experiment]]. In 1998, she transitioned to astroparticle physics and joined the [[Antarctic Muon And Neutrino Detector Array]], a neutrino telescope located at the South Pole.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Baerdemaeker |first=Siska De |title=Scientific Advisory Board - Oskar Klein Centre |url=https://www.okc.albanova.se/about-the-okc/scientific-advisory-board-1.643748?cache=1 |access-date=2025-06-26 |website=www.okc.albanova.se |language=en}}</ref>

Botner has held leadership positions in the international IceCube partnership, serving as spokesperson<ref>{{Cite news |last=Murray |first=Molly |date=2016-04-04 |title=UD part of bigger look at tiniest objects in space |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-news-journal-ud-part-of-bigger-look/174604486/ |access-date=2025-06-16 |work=The News Journal |pages=A2}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2013-11-30 |title=IceCube Pushes Neutrinos to the Forefront of Astronomy |url=http://spacenews.com/icecube-pushes-neutrinos-to-the-forefront-of-astronomy/ |access-date=2025-06-16 |website=SpaceNews |language=en-US}}</ref> from 2013 to 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bravo |first=Silvia |date=2017-05-16 |title=Olga Botner hands the spokesperson baton to Darren Grant |url=https://icecube.wisc.edu/news/collaboration/2017/05/olga-botner-hands-spokesperson-baton-to-darren-grant/ |access-date=2025-06-16 |website=IceCube |language=en-US}}</ref>

From 2010 until 2019 Botner served on the [[Nobel Prize]] committee for physics.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-11-27 |title=Exciting appointment in the Nobel Committee for Physics - Uppsala University |url=https://www.uu.se/en/news/2018/2018-11-27-exciting-appointment-in-the-nobel-committee-for-physics |access-date=2025-06-16 |website=www.uu.se |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
Botner is known for her work in multi-messenger astronomy, and her research has led to speculation that she will receive a Nobel Prize in physics.<ref>{{Cite news |date=3 October 2023 |title=Light or new materials tipped for Nobel Physics Prize |work=The New Vision; Kampala |id={{ProQuest|2871589646}}}}</ref> She has examined neutrino detection with the IceCube Neutrino Observatory serving as her main research platform. In 2017 Botner was part of the team that was able to track a neutrino measured at the IceCube observatory back to a [[blazar]] located 3.7 billion light years away.<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 12, 2018 |title=A 4 Billion Light-Year Journey Ends At The South Pole |work=National Public Radio, All Things Considered; Washington, D.C. |id={{ProQuest|2068775218}}}}</ref>

In 2023 she led work on a search for coincident neutrino emissions from [[fast radio burst]]s (FRBs). Botner, along with her collaborators, analyzed data from seven years of IceCube cascade events to investigate whether there was a correlation between fast radio bursts and neutrino signals, ultimately seeking to expand understanding of the mechanical processes behind these high-energy astrophysical occurrences.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Abbasi |first1=R. |last2=Ackermann |first2=M. |last3=Adams |first3=J. |last4=Agarwalla |first4=S. N. |last15=Bai |first15=X. |display-authors=1 |date=2023-04-01 |title=A Search for Coincident Neutrino Emission from Fast Radio Bursts with Seven Years of IceCube Cascade Events |journal=The Astrophysical Journal |volume=946 |issue=2 |pages=80 |doi=10.3847/1538-4357/acbea0 |doi-access=free |arxiv=2212.06702 |bibcode=2023ApJ...946...80A |issn=0004-637X}}</ref>

In another study, Botner worked to constrain high-energy neutrino emissions from supernovae, and her research helped elucidate the role of neutrinos in these explosive events, providing insights into supernova dynamics and the potential for neutrinos to serve as cosmic messengers.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Abbasi |first1=R. |last2=Ackermann |first2=M. |last3=Adams |first3=J. |last4=Agarwalla |first4=S. Botner's collaboration with the IceCube Neutrino Observatory has led to the development of IceCat-1, the IceCube Event Catalog of Alert Tracks which provides a comprehensive list of important neutrino events and aims to facilitate real-time observation and collaboration among researchers.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Abbasi |first1=R. |last2=Ackermann |first2=M. |last3=Adams |first3=J. |last4=Agarwalla |first4=S. Botner has also worked on gamma-ray bursts (GRBs). In 2024 Botner and her team used IceCube data to investigate high-energy neutrinos generated by gamma-ray bursts, which examined how these energetic bursts can be sources of cosmic neutrinos.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Abbasi |first1=R. |last2=Ackermann |first2=M. |last3=Adams |first3=J. |last4=Agarwalla |first4=S. == Honors and awards ==
In 2001<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Olga Botner - Uppsala universitet |url=https://www.uu.se/kontakt-och-organisation/personal?query=XX2728 |access-date=2025-06-16 |website=www.uu.se |language=sv}}</ref> Botner was elected member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Olga Botner |url=https://www.kva.se/en/contact/olga-botner-2/ |access-date=2025-06-16 |website=Kungl. Vetenskapsakademien |language=en-GB}}</ref> Botner, [[Fred Nyberg]], and [[Johan Svedjedal]] received the Rudbeck Medal from Uppsala University in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-21 |title=The Rudbeck Medal - Uppsala University |url=https://www.uu.se/en/about-uu/academic-traditions/traditions/the-rudbeck-medal |access-date=2025-06-26 |website=www.uu.se |language=en}}</ref>
